findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", allowing the service user to read/modify any bucket, launch or terminate any instance, and deploy arbitrary Lambda code. Compromise of this user's credentials results in near-complete account takeover and possible privilege escalation via lambda/ec2 role passing.

A permanent IAM access key is created for the user and its secret is stored in Terraform state in plaintext (no pgp_key is supplied, so `secret` is stored unencrypted). Anyone with read access to the state file obtains credentials with the broad permissions attached to this user.

No pgp_key is configured, so the `encrypted_secret` attribute will be empty and the raw secret access key is only available as an unencrypted state attribute, weakening protection of the credential at rest.

The `svc_deploy_key_material` output exports the access key secret material and is not marked `sensitive = true`, so it is printed to the console and CI logs and readable by anyone with access to plan/apply output or remote state outputs.

A long-lived IAM user with static keys is used for deployment rather than an assumable IAM role with short-lived STS credentials, and force_destroy = true allows silent removal of attached keys/policies. Combined with the wildcard policy this creates a high-value, non-rotating credential target.
